title: One scorer for all headline metrics
description:
As an evaluation owner, I want every headline metric to come from one matching function, so that fixture Jest, `benchmark:run`, and any precision helper cannot disagree on the same packet.

## Current mess

- **`tests/eval/score.ts`**: per-layer finding bags, `identity.ts` matching, path normalize, union of exhaustive scopes per fixture+layer, data-items identity-only, optional `finding.layer` tags.
- **`tests/benchmark/precision.ts`**: exact `finding.key === annotation.subject.key`, no taxonomy aliases, no layer tags, different overlap helper. Still used by `corpus-precision.spec.ts`.
- **Public `dataparade-cli`**: leftover eval/score/identity copy. The next `cli-v*` rsync from the app monorepo does not update scanner, but humans will still run the wrong tree.
- **Plexus** `evaluate accuracy` / `evaluate_recall`: third client, was not runnable in the last pass (proxy/backend mode). If it comes back with yet another identity rule, we will have four numbers.

`scanRepoByManifestLayers` comments claim personal-data matching runs at most once; the body can call `collectPersonalDataFindings` three times (mentions, raw-hits, data-items). That is a runner bug adjacent to “one scorer” (same scan, one finding inventory).

## Why it blocks scanner work

A “fix” that greens `benchmark:run` and reds `precision.ts` (or the reverse) is not a fix. Agents will pick the number that supports the patch.

## Questions to answer

- Is `scoreEvalCases` the only matcher? Then `precision.ts` becomes a thin wrapper or dies.
- Does corpus CI call `run-benchmark` (materialize is opt-in) or only YAML load tests? What is the official command for headline numbers?
- After identity (task 1) and unread (task 2) land, which tests are the contract suite that must not be forked?
- Do we delete or archive eval code on `dataparade-cli` so it cannot rot into a second origin?

## Not this task

Do not add a fourth metrics pipeline (new notebooks, ad-hoc scripts) while this is open.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Decision

There is one canonical evaluator and one matching contract for every headline result. `scoreEvalCases` may remain the public entry point, but it must consume canonical observations from the shared adapters. `tests/benchmark/precision.ts` is deleted or reduced to a thin call into that evaluator; it may not own matching rules.

Matching is deterministic and cardinality-aware. The evaluator performs one-to-one assignment between expected observations and findings, preferring exact canonical identity and stronger evidence matches. One finding cannot satisfy several gold cases, and duplicate findings cannot all receive true-positive credit from one gold case. Unmatched evaluable positives are false negatives; unmatched findings in closed scope are false positives. Repository-level entity layers consolidate repeated evidence into one expected entity before assignment.

Closed-world scope is packet-and-layer metadata with review provenance, independent of positive annotations. This permits an exhaustively reviewed layer with zero positives to penalize hallucinated findings. Scope must not be stored only by repeating it on positive records.

The official headline path is the scanner repository command, accepted gold only, deterministic inference configuration with AI disabled, and validated pinned materializations. The contract suite includes synthetic golden inputs/outputs for identity, labels, eligibility, scope, one-to-one matching, duplicates, zero-positive scopes, and path normalization.

The public CLI and Plexus must call the shared evaluator through a library or stable JSON/process boundary. Copied scoring trees are removed or clearly archived as non-authoritative.

The adjacent runner defect is follow-on work: personal-data matching runs once per repo and the raw-hit, mention, and data-item projections derive from that one inventory.

Rejected alternatives:

- independent any-match loops for recall and precision;
- greedy order-dependent reuse of findings;
- separate corpus, Jest, CLI, or Plexus scorers;
- positive-attached scope as the only closed-world declaration;
- ad-hoc notebooks or scripts as headline sources.

Scorer implementation follows the identity, eligibility, and layer-unit decisions and must not retune detectors.
